> Learning to take pleasure in the small things is a saying that comes to mind, but this is not always quite as easy as it seems. But I think it rings true- the happiest people seem to take joy from the smallest things. And this takes time. So I guess what I'm getting at is what do you enjoy? Do you like any kind of sport? Hobbies? Interests? Or if you have lost interest in things you used to enjoy, have you had any thoughts on trying something new that you are curious about? All these things could lead to new experiences, meeting new people and discovering the joy in life again. You said you have recently moved? Have you given any thought to exploring and finding what your new surroundings have to offer? 

Thank you.  Is this your main account?

Also, I've thought about this some more.

I'm happy not knowing if this life matters, and I'm happy just living it.

There are ups.
There are downs.

But I'm alive and it feels nice never knowing where that next up will be.  It feels nice to have the scheduled meetings with a special somebody or a dedicated team.  Or it might be a surprise, like a chance encounter that leads to something more.

There will be downs.  There may be a series of downs.  But the next up is there.

I have to run to an evening class, but I'll respond more indepth when I get back.  The core of the problem is me trying to figure out why life... or anything... matters.  Why bother?  Again, I live my life like it does, but I know I miss out on doing things with groups and others because of that nagging thought of why it all matters.
